name: BotLab Dynamics
hq_regions: New Delhi, India; operates across India, APAC, Middle East, Africa
fleet_scale_claim: Reported figures vary across their own materials: "500+ shows across 200+ cities" (company blog) and "700+ performances" (homepage); flew 5,500 drones at the Amaravati Drone Summit 2024 (5 Guinness World Records) and 3,500 in 2023, per third-party aggregation (Tracxn/The Machine Maker)
notable_shows: 5,500-drone Amaravati Drone Summit 2024 (5 Guinness World Records); 1,000-drone Rashtrapati Bhavan show
waiver_status: Not applicable -- no evidence of any US operation or FAA filing found; activity is India/Asia/Middle East-focused

name: Celestial
hq_regions: UK, with a US office; flies from a private airfield in Somerset, England
fleet_scale_claim: "The largest fleet of drones in the UK -- over 1,000," grown from a starting fleet of 20, per Celestial's own site; shows run 500-1,500 drones per performance
notable_shows: Clients include Nike, Disney, Samsung, Eurovision, Glastonbury; Super Bowl LA activation and an Avatar 3 premiere per The Drone Girl's roundup
waiver_status: Not publicly stated -- UK company; no CAA-equivalent or FAA waiver documentation found for any US operations

name: Dronisos
hq_regions: Bordeaux, France (HQ) + Orlando, FL (US office); operates in 30+ countries
fleet_scale_claim: "Up to 5,000 drones simultaneously outdoors" per Dronisos's own FAQ; runs its own "Dronisos Academy" pilot training pipeline in Bordeaux and near Orlando
notable_shows: Disneyland Paris "Cascade of Lights"; Tour de France 2024 Nice finish; 1,495-drone Bastille Day show; publicly confirmed as direct organizer of Orlando's 2023 Christmas Drone Show
waiver_status: FAA Certificate of Waiver 107W-2022-00614 (responsible person Laurent Perchais) confirmed for night/twilight ops and multi-aircraft single-pilot operation -- effective through May 2024; no renewed/successor certificate found, so current live-waiver status is unconfirmed

name: Firefly Drone Shows
hq_regions: Detroit, MI; services all of the U.S. plus international
fleet_scale_claim: "200 to 1,000+ drones" per show; "Full in-house manufacturing and maintenance" -- builds and maintains its own drones, batteries, components, and firmware. Also operates a separate hardware-sales sister brand, Firefly Drone Systems, which sells/leases the same platform to other operators -- distinct from Firefly Drone Shows' own direct-production business
notable_shows: States it "produces over 300 shows each year"; 250-drone World Scout Jamboree show (80,000 attendees); 400-drone Ford Rouge Plant 100th-anniversary show; $18,000/200-drone Sterling Heights, MI Sterlingfest 2026 show
waiver_status: FAA Certificate of Waiver 107W-2025-02052 confirmed (night ops, up to 2,500 drones by one operator); a second event-specific certificate 107W-2024-04184 also found

name: Geoscan
hq_regions: St. Petersburg, Russia; shows also flown in Taiwan, Thailand, India, Moldova, Cyprus, Tunisia
fleet_scale_claim: Manufacturer that also directly produces its own shows; ran a 2,198-drone show (2020) and a 2,500-drone show (2025), both self-published but consistent with third-party GPS World coverage of Geoscan's positioning tech in these shows
notable_shows: 2,198-drone Victory Day 75th anniversary show (2020); 2,500-drone 80th anniversary show (2025)
waiver_status: Not applicable -- Russian regulatory context, not FAA; no US operations found

name: Great Lakes Drone Company (dba Starlight Drone Shows / Starlight Aerial Productions)
fleet_scale_claim: "Hundreds of drones," shows staged in sets of 25-500+; FAA-authorized to fly "hundreds of drones with one operator." No public claim of in-house drone manufacture was found (contrast with Firefly/Dronisos/BotLab) -- they have used at least one third-party drone model (the Lumenier ARORA)
notable_shows: EAA AirVenture 2026 night shows; $40,000/200-drone SeaTac, WA show (2024, partial failure -- 55 drones lost, vendor offered a full refund); $10,000 Eden Prairie, MN show (2024, via the Starlight Aerial Productions brand)
waiver_status: Confirmed: holds FAA Waiver 2022-P107-00689 (blanket Class G approval) and a more recent Certificate of Waiver 107W-2026-00697 (responsible person Matthew Quinn) for operations over people and above 400 ft AGL

name: HighGreat
hq_regions: Shenzhen, China; performances in 300+ cities internationally
fleet_scale_claim: Manufacturer that also directly produces its own shows; "over 8,000 performances in more than 300 cities" per aggregated press coverage; states manufacturing capacity up to 1M units/year
notable_shows: 5,200/5,000+ drone Guinness-record event (Oct. 2022), independently covered by sUAS News and DroneDJ
waiver_status: Not applicable -- Chinese manufacturer/operator; no US operations or FAA filings found

name: Lumasky
fleet_scale_claim: Company claims an 18,000-drone fleet across "213 projects in 41 countries" (self-reported, not independently audited)
notable_shows: 9,000-drone Disneyland Abu Dhabi show, covered by Interesting Engineering
waiver_status: Not applicable -- UAE-based; no FAA relevance found

name: Nova Sky Stories
hq_regions: Boulder, CO (HQ); operates globally (Middle East, UK, USA, APAC, Europe)
fleet_scale_claim: Acquired the Intel Shooting Star drone program outright in 2022 (a real hardware/business acquisition, not a license); "more than 9,000 drones," with a 2025 funding round earmarked to scale to 25,000 units
notable_shows: Vatican "Grace for the World"; FIFA 2025 Club World Cup (Miami/NJ); Abu Dhabi Dept. of Culture partnership for up to 10,000 simultaneous drones; historical Shooting Star lineage includes the 2017 Super Bowl and 2021 Tokyo Olympics
waiver_status: Confirmed: a standing multi-drone/night waiver, a 14 CFR 107.36 exemption for the Nova Star Drone V3/V3.1 (through Aug. 2027), and Certificate of Waiver 107W-2026-01198

name: Open Sky Pro (Open Sky Productions)
hq_regions: Salt Lake City, UT; markets into many US states including Florida
fleet_scale_claim: "100 to over 500 synchronized drones" per show, "up to 1,000 drones for special projects"; claims delivery "across 35 states" and "well over 5 million guests" reached
notable_shows: Minden-Tahoe SkyFest; named clients include Kyocera, HOKA, Summerfest, Steamboat; $66,000/200-drone Port Orange, FL show and $95,000/300-drone Flagstaff, AZ show
waiver_status: Company claims operating "under a Part 107.35 waiver" on its own marketing pages; not independently verified against an FAA docket number

name: Pixis Drones
hq_regions: Alexandria, VA (HQ); satellite offices in Atlanta, Austin, Chicago, LA, Las Vegas, Miami, Nashville, NYC
fleet_scale_claim: A federal court record (Pixis Drones, LLC v. Lumenier LLC, D. Del. Civil Action No. 23-141-RGA) confirms Pixis commissioned custom, exclusive-use drone hardware from contract manufacturers (first Lumenier, later Uvify) -- documented evidence of owning a proprietary fleet, not reselling a turnkey show
notable_shows: Super Bowl LVI activation; 2022 NBA Draft; 2023 NFL Draft; NY Giants 100th Season Fan Fest; ~80+ shows listed on its own site (2020-2025)
waiver_status: FAA Waiver 107W-2026-00717 confirmed, name-matched to Pixis Drones LLC, Alexandria VA (altitude relief under 14 CFR 107.51(b))

name: Sky Elements
hq_regions: Coppell, TX; states it flies "60% of All Known U.S. Drone Shows"
fleet_scale_claim: "We own/operate the largest fleet of drones in the United States" per its own About page, corroborated by independent press citing a fleet of roughly 3,000 drones; largest single deployment cited: 3,050 drones over F1 Monaco
notable_shows: "Stranger Things" show billed as largest U.S. drone show; Nashville Fourth of July; Seattle Seahawks halftime; first U.S. company approved to fly pyrotechnics on drones
waiver_status: Held a named FAA pyro/night-ops waiver, publicly suspended by the FAA after a December 2024 Orlando incident that injured a child, then reinstated for specific venues and updated (Jan. 2026) to incorporate DLSA Tier 1 safety-standard requirements -- extensively documented in press under Sky Elements' own name

name: SkyMagic
hq_regions: Leeds, UK (primary base) + offices in Singapore, Dover DE (USA), Abu Dhabi; delivered shows in 25+ territories since 2015
fleet_scale_claim: "Develops and manufactures all its UAVs, as well as tech and software used to navigate the performing swarms," with in-house design/production -- the strongest vertical-integration claim of any operator in this directory; fleet of roughly 1,400 LED swarm drones plus a newer "laser drone" line
notable_shows: King Charles III coronation; Zayed International Airport A380-landing show; Netflix "Troll 2"/"Rebel Moon" at Sphere; "over 11,000 flying hours" claimed
waiver_status: No specific, named CAA authorization, Operational Safety Case, or UK SORA Operational Authorisation could be found publicly for SkyMagic -- unconfirmed either way, not evidence of noncompliance

name: Skyworx Drone Shows
hq_regions: US-based (founded by Taylor Woodall); operates across US, Mexico, Canada
fleet_scale_claim: "One of the largest fleets in the industry," "150 to over 1,500 drones" per show; press explicitly attributes fleet ownership/operation to Skyworx with Damoda (a Chinese swarm-control supplier) named as a disclosed hardware/tech partner, not the operator of record
notable_shows: 10,197-drone display (Sept. 2024, aerial-image world record); 1,200-drone CES 2026 show; Netflix Is a Joke Festival (1,700 drones); National Bank Open Canada (500 drones)
waiver_status: An active, docket-identifiable FAA exemption petition (FAA-2025-2314, filed under the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024) confirmed under Skyworx's name; a separate Certificate of Waiver 107W-2026-01055 also on record

name: Verge Aero
hq_regions: Austin, TX; partner network in 50+ countries
fleet_scale_claim: Primarily a drone-show hardware+software platform sold/licensed to other operators ("Buy a Drone Show Fleet," #PoweredByVerge partner network, no royalty fees) -- but Verge Aero's own site also documents it directly flying client shows with its own named staff (e.g. a Rice University presidential-inauguration show, staffed by Verge's own "Director of Show Operations" and "Project Manager"), and it has a documented history of directly producing the Philadelphia Eagles' in-stadium shows. Included here on the strength of that direct-operation evidence, with this dual role flagged rather than hidden
notable_shows: Rice University presidential inauguration (flown directly by Verge Aero staff); historical Philadelphia Eagles in-stadium shows
waiver_status: Not publicly stated for Verge Aero's own direct-production shows specifically; the company's platform customers hold their own independent waivers
